newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes fraction up, helped by lending.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes fraction up, helped by lending.

text.p: Gold prices were little changed at the afternoon official fixing from slightly lower opening levels on Tuesday.
Dealers said New York opened in line with the London market, which had earlier drifted lower following overnight selling in the U.S. and Asian markets.
A brisk lending market helped lift the Comex August contract to $322.10 an ounce, a gain of $1.30 by the fixing.
But dealers said the trend remained towards lower prices.
Gold was fixed at $319.75 per ounce, up $0.75 from this morning and compared to $321.70 on Monday afternoon. London closed on Monday at $320.60/$321.10.
Dealers said the speculative pressure on gold started late on Monday after it failed to beat resistance at $322.50.
Then Australian producer selling emerged during Asian trading hours, which also helped depress prices.
"The threat of producer and central bank sales is going to continue capping the market," a dealer said.

Chartists said prices were concluding a week-long sideways movement and should now move to probe last week's 12-year lows after failing to challenge $322/$323 per ounce resistance over the past few days.
"It is looking like a bear flag...it should retest and break below the $313.60 low," said technical analyst Karen Jones of Credit Suisse First Boston.
Analysts said gold's first downside target would be the $315 area and then the 12-year low of $313.60 hit last week.
News that Australia's central bank had sold 167 tonnes from its gold reserves sent prices spiralling lower as investors pulled out of the market and speculators bet prices would sink still further.
Silver was off its intraday highs at $4.32/$4.34, still up three cents on a bearish close.
A drop below the $4.23 low of last week would leave silver vulnerable to decline to the September 1993 low of $3.88, analysts said.
Platinum and palladium went in opposite directions, with platinum around $1.00 lower at $404.50/$408.50 and palladium $6.50 firmer at $172.70/$176.70.
Russia's metal export agency Almazjuvelirexport confirmed it had resumed long-delayed deliveries of platinum group metals to Japan and said the first supplies left Russia on July 8.
